text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user asks for a subjective recommendation on which player to build a team around, based on the previously computed points/rebounds/assists per game leaderboard, rather than requesting new data.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"Based on the leaderboard, James Harden stands out as the best building block: he leads in points per game (29.28) among qualified players (20+ games) while also contributing strong assists (9.69/game) and solid rebounding (6.72/game), showing he can both score at an elite level and create for teammates. Russell Westbrook is a close second and arguably more well-rounded statistically (27.07 pts, 10.45 ast, 9.37 reb per game, near triple-double averages), which could make him the choice if you value all-around production and playmaking over pure scoring. DeMarcus Cousins offers a different profile (26.71 pts, 11.44 reb) with dominant rebounding but far fewer assists, better suited as a scoring-and-rebounding anchor than a primary playmaker. If the priority is a single go-to scorer who also facilitates, Harden is the strongest pick; if you want a hub who elevates teammates across multiple categories, Westbrook is the stronger foundation."}
